chunks: From him, from al-Mitham, from Aban, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If a free person confesses to himself regarding slavery, do we enslave him based on that?' He said: 'He is a slave if he confesses to himself.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a free person confesses to being a slave?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-ijaz* (voluntary acceptance) in manumission, ruling that a free person who confesses to being a slave is legally bound by that admission. This highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in personal status law, where individual consent can alter one's legal standing, reflecting the broader Islamic legal maxim that 'the word of a person against himself is evidence.'
